newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 5.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 5.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:
* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 42.49 points to 7,269.66 as investors braced for the May jobs report due on Friday.

* Indonesia's inflation slowed in May while the trade surplus fell significantly in March but officials said on Wednesday the economy was in good shape. Information Minister Harmoko said on Wednesday after a monthly cabinet meeting that inflation rose 0.19 percent month-on-month in May, compared with an increase of 0.56 percent in April.

* Speaker of the House of Representatives Wahono said on Wednesday that the house will amend its rules and regulations but did not say whether the move was prompted by the poor performance of the badly split minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) during last Thursday's general election.
* Indonesia'a ruling Golkar party won an unprecedented re-vote on Madura island on Wednesday forced by angry Moslems who burned ballot boxes claiming fraud after last week's polls.
MARKET

* On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index closed down 4.86 points at 693.54 after hitting an intra-day low of 690.52 points, dragged down by profit-taking in blue chip counters, particularly heavyweight Telkom, brokers said.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,428.50/29.50 at 0200 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.00/30.00.
STOCKS TO WATCH

* National Development Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Wednesday that since April the national Timor car has been the government's official car. Timor car is produced by PT Timor Putra Nasional in cooperation with Kia Motors of South Korea. The move might dampen sentiment on car-makers Astra International and Bimantara.

* PT Indonesia Satellite (Indosat) on reports that it will launch on Thursday its the Global Express Phone-7 service or the Inmarsat Mini-M, a new international call service using International Maritime Satellite's (Inmarsat) network.
* Cigarette maker PT Gudang Garam on market speculation that its first quarter would be slightly lower than market expectations.
* Bakrie & Brothers following Tuesday's reports that its unit, PT Bakrie Motor will start to sell vans by December 1997.

* Flexible-packaging firm PT Argha Karya Prima Industry on news that it had signed a memorandum of understanding to sell some of its fixed assets and inventory to German packaging materials manufacturer VAW Europack GmbH of the Viag group.
* Adhesive producer Kurnia Kapuas Utama on market talk that an affiliate company would take a controlling stake in the firm.
* Tyre-maker PT Gajah Tunggal following a company announcement that it had signed an agreement with Pirelli Tire's North American subsidiary to manufacture Pirelli car radial tyres.
* Information technology and computer distributor Astra Graphia on reports that it will soon market an Internet facility.

* Shipping and sea transportation company PT Berlian Laju Tanker on a news report the company had indicated a first quarter net profit of five billion rupiah, or 20 percent higher from the same period last year.
* Property firm Lippo Land on reports that the firm will buy a 15 percent stake in its sister company Lippo Karawaci from the market.
* Property firm Surya Semesta Internusa on continued market talk of the possible entry of a local conglomerate or foreign investor into the firm.
* Life insurance Lippo Life following its proposed rights issue which is subject to shareholders approval at its extraordinary shareholders' meeting on June 27.
